track.legalName: Consolidated Multi-Record Sealing Petition in the Boston Municipal Court Department
track.publicName: Sealing several dismissed cases at once in Boston

citations: Boston Municipal Court Department Amended Standing Order No. 1-09
controllingAuthority.summary: The Boston Municipal Court Department permits a single consolidated petition to seal three or more criminal records from two or more BMC divisions, under a Standing Order revised after Pon to conform to the new legal standard. It is a local implementation of the ordinary § 100C judicial-sealing remedy, not a separate statewide remedy. Below the threshold, the ordinary route applies with one form per case.

exclusions: Records outside the Boston Municipal Court Department. This does not reach District Court, Juvenile Court or Superior Court records.
Fewer than three criminal records, or records from fewer than two BMC divisions. Below that threshold the ordinary judicial sealing route applies with one form per case.

Records that ended in a finding of no probable cause or a not-guilty finding are outside this consolidated procedure: the May 10, 2024 amended Standing Order 1-09 limits it to dismissal and nolle prosequi records under the second paragraph of G.L. c. 276, § 100C. Those other dispositions arise under a different paragraph of § 100C and their separate procedural and case-law treatment is not decided here; they are not called ineligible for every form of relief (recorded 2026-09-06 from the owner-relayed research).

waitingPeriods.condition: Dismissal, nolle prosequi, no probable cause or not guilty
waitingPeriods.duration: None, the same as the ordinary judicial sealing route.

geography.venue: Boston Municipal Court Department only, keyed by the Standing Order to the division in whose territorial jurisdiction the person resides, read with the general BMC rule that a person no longer residing in BMC territory files in the division where the most recent eligible record is from.

destination.name: Boston Municipal Court division identified by the Standing Order
destination.detail: A consolidated petition supplements rather than replaces the statewide form. The judge may request additional information or documents about the listed cases from the Clerk-Magistrate or the Probation Department.

components.notes: Consolidated petition to seal multiple criminal records, drafted against the required contents and procedure of BMC Amended Standing Order No. 1-09 and the Pon standard, listing every qualifying BMC record across divisions.

Threshold and venue instruction: three or more records from two or more BMC divisions, filed in the division where the person resides or, if they no longer live in BMC territory, where the most recent eligible record is from. Preliminary hearing, public notice and final hearing follow.

rules.filing: File the consolidated petition in the BMC division identified by the Standing Order's residence-based venue rule (the division covering the petitioner's residence; for a non-resident, the division of the most recent applicable criminal record).
rules.fees: No filing fee: the Massachusetts Court System's guide states that requesting sealing has no fee (MA2). Recorded 2026-09-06 from the owner-relayed research; before that date this rule read 'None identified in the review.'
rules.feeWaiver: Not applicable: no filing fee is charged for a request to seal.
rules.notice: The petitioner sends a copy of the petition to the Suffolk County District Attorney's Office at least 30 days before the final hearing unless that office waives the full notice period, and keeps proof of what was sent and when; the court's own notice to the Commonwealth does not remove that obligation. A preliminary hearing is discretionary and the court may proceed directly to a single final hearing; public notice and the final hearing follow under the Standing Order. Any evidence-of-service fields are product completion fields, not a claim that a separately named statutory certificate is universally required. (Recorded 2026-09-06 from the owner-relayed research; previously 'Preliminary hearing, public notice and final hearing per the Standing Order.')
rules.service: The petitioner's own 30-day notice to the Suffolk County District Attorney's Office before the final hearing, unless waived by that office; proof of what was sent and when is kept. (Previously 'Per the Standing Order.')

researchConsolidationScope.statement: The May 10, 2024 amended Standing Order 1-09 limits this consolidation procedure to at least three dismissal or nolle-prosequi criminal records from at least two BMC divisions under § 100C's second paragraph; the Judiciary guide recommends rather than universally requires criminal records or certified dockets. The guide's stop when any hearing is set is a product boundary and is retained; supporting an ordinary uncontested hearing is a separate decision from correctly explaining the published process.

researchFormIdentity.statement: The Standing Order authorizes one petition and says a form is available, but an exact current dedicated consolidated form was not retrieved by the research. Neither unsupported universal assertion is perpetuated: that no such court form exists, or that a TC0057 must accompany every case. The accepted instrument, and whether any per-case forms are required for the selected court, remain to be confirmed with the issuing court; the existing release blocker on form identity stays.

researchParticipantText.text:
Scope. Use this consolidated route for at least three criminal records ending in dismissal or nolle prosequi across at least two BMC divisions. Other dispositions require their own treatment. Confirm the proper filing division and list each applicable docket.

Fee and notice. There is no filing fee to request sealing. Send a copy of this petition to the Suffolk County District Attorney's Office at least 30 days before the final hearing unless that office waives the full notice period. Keep proof of what you sent and when. Court notice to the Commonwealth does not eliminate your separate obligation. Follow the hearing notice; a separate preliminary hearing is not always held.

selfHelpStopConditions: The threshold of three or more records from two or more BMC divisions is not met, in which case the ordinary route applies with one form per case.
Records fall outside the Boston Municipal Court Department.
The judge requests additional information about the listed cases.

unresolvedQuestions.question: Whether the Boston Municipal Court publishes a dedicated form for the consolidated multi-record petition. The Standing Order prescribes contents and procedure but no published form was established, so a controlled custom pleading is used against those required contents.

provenance.sourceStatement: Is an official form mandatory? Unresolved. The Standing Order prescribes contents and procedure; whether BMC publishes a form was not established.

legalDesignDecision.rationale: Classified as a local_variant non-relief node under the adopted memorandum: the BMC multi-record procedure implements the ordinary § 100C judicial-sealing track locally and is not a separate statewide remedy, so the underlying relief is not double-counted. Re-reviewed under the packet-only model and classified as a single custom_pleading rather than a composed route: the review's stage 1 is threshold and venue routing rather than a legal unit, and stage 3 is hearings, which are post-generation handoffs. No published BMC form was established, and the Standing Order supplies the required contents and procedure, so a controlled consolidated pleading is generated with a local-form override.

limitations.statement: Never use sealing and expungement interchangeably in Massachusetts copy. Sealing does not destroy the record; expungement does.

provenance.sourceStatement: Massachusetts sealing does not destroy the record. Expungement does. Never use the two interchangeably in Massachusetts copy.
